note: Real, public sources only. Each quote is copied word for word from the linked page and each claim uses only numbers that quote states. Vendor sources are marked vendor_reported. Kinds with no source we could verify (slow_response, booking_friction, no_website, no_phone, no_hours, pricing, refunds) show none. Re-check with: node scripts/verify-case-studies.mjs

studies.title: Study: Replying to Customer Reviews Results in Better Ratings
studies.claim: Hotels that started replying to reviews got 12% more reviews and ratings 0.12 stars higher on average.
studies.quote: When hotels start responding, they receive 12% more reviews and their ratings increase by an average of 0.12 stars (on a 1-to-5 scale).
studies.caveat: Hotels on TripAdvisor, not home services.

studies.title: Local Consumer Review Survey 2026
studies.claim: 42% of consumers surveyed say they are unlikely to use a business that never replies to reviews.
studies.quote: 42% say they’re unlikely to use a business that never replies.
studies.caveat: A survey of what people say they would do. Vendor-reported: read the method on the linked page.

studies.title: The Pitfalls of Review Solicitation: Evidence from a Natural Experiment on TripAdvisor
studies.authors: Baojun Gao, Jing Wang, Xiaojie Ding, Yue Guo
studies.claim: Hotels that asked guests for reviews got 34.3% more reviews and a 0.151 higher rating, with shorter reviews.
studies.quote: hotels’ participation in the review solicitation program results in a 34.3% increase in review volume, a 0.151 increase in review rating, but a 16.9% decrease in review length.
studies.caveat: The same paper finds unprompted reviews fell 15.5% once hotels started asking.

studies.title: Understanding and Overcoming Biases in Customer Reviews
studies.claim: Verified customers asked for a review by email rated up to 0.5 star higher than people who reviewed on their own.
studies.quote: verified customers who are prompted (by an email) to write a review, submit, on average, up to 0.5 star higher ratings than self-motivated web reviewers.
studies.caveat: Online retail reviews, not local services.

studies.title: 2019 Home Service Call Performance Report
studies.claim: Home service owners thought they answered 97% of calls; on average only 66% were answered.
studies.quote: Business owners estimated they had a call answer rate of 97%, when in reality only 66% of calls were answered on average.
studies.caveat: Vendor-reported: read the method on the linked page.

studies.title: Reviews, Reputation, and Revenue: The Case of Yelp.com
studies.claim: One more Yelp star went with 5 to 9 percent more revenue for the restaurants studied.
studies.quote: a one-star increase in Yelp rating leads to a 5-9 percent increase in revenue
studies.caveat: Restaurants on Yelp; the paper says the effect is driven by independent restaurants, not chains. Working Paper 12-016, revised March 2016.
